reason: Clustered is an EXACT synonym of PATO aggregated; 'sparsely' is a degree qualifier kept in the record. The Spanish 'algo esparcidas' is a stray (scattered) and should not be grounded by this rule.
Vesiculous/vésiculeux/vesiculoso is the same word as vesicular, whose synonyms already include vesiculose; mericarp, calyx and fruit are among its listed bearers.
Bicarpellary = made of two carpels: a count of carpel (PO_0009030) = 2 with the counted part in the word, like '3-foliolate'.
'Secondary veins subtangent to the margin' relates the veins to a second part (the leaf margin); it is not a quality of the vein on its own, and 'sub-' adds the approximate qualifier.

A function, not a morphological quality, and the statements are heterogeneous (secretory cells of a hair, wood parenchyma, leaves secreting); secretory hairs and glands are already handled by the bearer rules glandular trichome (PO_0004509) and portion of secretory tissue (PO_0005656).
Same as the previous rule 'expanded' (C181) -> dilated; 'slightly' is a degree qualifier kept in the record.
For anthers, lateral dehiscence is latrorse, whose synonyms already list 'laterally dehiscent' and 'déhiscence latérale'. Restrict the rule to anther/stamen; the fruit statements are left out.

A part, not a quality; 'sin estaminodios' then gives staminode absent by pattern 15.
A half-superior ovary is one whose lower part is fused with the receptacle and upper part free, which is the definition of half-inferior.

A trichome-type term used with different senses across families (multi-tiered stellate hairs in Solanum, spiny hairs elsewhere) and stated of the hairs, not of the organ; no single definition can be given safely from these examples.
Same as the previous rule 'obscure' (C174) -> inconspicuous, with the bearer secondary leaf vein (PO_0020140) taken from 'lateral veins'.
A misspelling of triplinerved; the examples all read 'triplinerved'.

label: pinnate-fibrillose
definition: A fibrous quality inhering in a leaf sheath by virtue of the thin front of the sheath breaking up into fibres that diverge on either side of a central line, like the barbs of a feather.
reason: A diagnostic Carex sheath character with no PATO or FLOPO term; fibrous alone loses the pinnate arrangement of the fibres.

label: epistomatic
definition: A spatial pattern quality inhering in a leaf or leaf blade by virtue of its stomata being confined to the adaxial (upper) surface.
reason: A standard leaf-anatomy character (grasses) with no term; like paracytic (FLOPO:0991332), it is a pattern of stomata, which is why it sits under spatial pattern.
'Base dilated' is the quality dilated with the bearer plant organ base (FLOPO_0985024) of the part described, as rules C181 and C267.

A character name, not a value: the colour word ('green') is the quality and the midrib, a synonym of leaf midvein, is the bearer. For scales and glumes the midrib is not strictly a leaf midvein and should stay review.
Distant is defined as 'widely separated from the nearest structures of its kind' and already has 'widely spaced' as a synonym.

target: docs/odp/00-part-and-quality.md (two annotations: lyrate FLOPO:0991057 and pinnatisect FLOPO:0991155)
reason: Both values hold: lyrate is defined as 'pinnately lobed or divided' with a large terminal lobe, and pinnatisect gives the depth of incision.
A carrot-like root is a thick taproot tapering evenly from the top, i.e. conical; napiform (FLOPO:0991306) is the turnip shape and does not fit.

target: docs/odp/00-part-and-quality.md (two annotations: pilose FLOPO:0991048 with a 'minutely' qualifier, and trichome star shaped PATO_0002065)
reason: A compound of the indument (minutely pilose) and the hair form (stellate) that both hold; no single term is needed.
An inflorescence with a racemose (indeterminate) main axis and cymose lateral units is a thyrse, as the Spanish 'cimoso-tirsoide' says.
Relational: PATO 'parallel to' (PATO_0002272) towards the axis (stem) that bears the leaves; the second term is in the statement.
'Sub-' is the approximate qualifier on pinnatipartite (FLOPO:0991156), as for 'suborbicular'.
'Umbels racemosely arranged' is the arrangement of partial inflorescences along an axis, a quality of the whole towards its parts; raceme-like (FLOPO:0991197) is defined for flowers, not for umbels.
States the absence of a part, pattern 15.

target: new: difference between the two halves of a part
reason: A measured asymmetry (the offset between the two sides of the blade base, in mm), not a quality word; it needs a measurement of length towards the other half, with asymmetrical (PATO_0000616) as its qualitative parent.

target: docs/odp/00-part-and-quality.md (two annotations: gland-dotted FLOPO:0991174 on the part, and black PATO_0000317 on its glands)
reason: Glandular-punctate is already a synonym of gland-dotted; 'black' is the colour of the dots, a second annotation of the glands, not a new term.
A part plus an attribute: the bearer is the glandular trichome (as rule C396), and the length is a measurement of it as a part of the organ named.
A shape between orbicular (PATO_0001934) and ovate (FLOPO:0991024), the compound-shape case like 'linear-lanceolate'.
